finding.title: The cross-thread SetFocus in the handoff can block past the 3 s settle deadline
finding.claim: The handoff calls SetFocus(parent) while attached to the WebView2 browser UI thread. Win32 sends WM_KILLFOCUS and WM_SETFOCUS to that thread's windows synchronously, with no timeout. The 3 s deadline is checked only after SetFocus returns.
finding.evidence: The deadline check (line 124) runs only after the handoff branch finishes. No other call in the loop (GetGUIThreadInfo, GetClassName, IsChild, GetParent, QueryInformationJobObject) can wait on the target thread. In round 47 the WebView2 thread always pumped messages (wm_null=ok:0ms), and SetFocus finished within 14 ms of the wait failure in hv-4 (trace lines 78783 to 78797).
finding.failure_scenario: The msedgewebview2 browser UI thread stops pumping messages while focus is on Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND. SetFocus never returns, so the settle cannot fail at its 3 s bound, and the guest's 300 s WithinBudget is not checked either. The run ends only at the host's work deadline: it still fails closed, but not at the settle's own deadline as the bounded-wait rule requires.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. It is real but minor.

What the code does (scripts/windows11/windows11_owned.cs, lines 98 to 127): SettleKeyboardFocus is a polling loop, and its 3 s deadline (FocusSettleMilliseconds) is checked only at line 124. When focus is on Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND, the handoff branch runs first: AttachThreadInput(own, focusThread, true) at line 115, then SetFocus(parent) at line 116. focusThread is the msedgewebview2 browser UI thread that owns both WebView2 windows, and line 112 requires the parent to be on that same thread.

Why it can block: the Win32 documentation says SetFocus sends WM_KILLFOCUS to the window losing focus and WM_SETFOCUS to the window gaining it. Both windows belong to that other thread. A message sent to another thread blocks until that thread processes it, and there is no timeout. So if the WebView2 UI thread stops pumping messages, SetFocus does not return, and line 124 is never reached. The other calls in the loop do not wait on another thread: GetForegroundWindow, GetWindowThreadProcessId, GetGUIThreadInfo, IsChild, GetClassName and GetParent, plus Members() (a job-object query) and AttachThreadInput itself. So the claim that only SetFocus can overrun the 3 s bound holds.

The guest's WithinBudget (300 s, windows11_guest.ps1 line 61) is checked only between PowerShell steps, so it cannot interrupt the blocked .NET call either. The run ends at the host work deadline in windows11_vm.py (owner.work_deadline, lines 711 and 843: "Actual Windows setup/guest deadline expired"), which fails closed.

Why this is NON_BLOCKING:
1. There is no false pass. If SetFocus returns after 3 s, the same iteration sets held=0 and then throws at line 124. If it never returns, the host deadline fails the run. That meets the project rule as stated in its own parenthesis: "fail closed, never pass on timeout".
2. The scenario needs a hung WebView2 browser UI thread. Round 47 never saw one: every probe in hv-1, hv-4 and hv-5 diag-focus.txt and diag-waits.txt shows hung=0 and wm_null=ok:0ms. The three diagnostic REMEDY handoffs all completed (REMEDY-OK in hv-4 diag-focus.txt).
3. The same kind of unguarded synchronous call already exists in reviewed code. Settles() calls UIA's FocusedElement inside its polling loop, and Keys() calls button.SetFocus() before the settle. Neither is bounded inside the loop by its own deadline.

What is genuinely inaccurate: KI-0184's resolution text says the owner "waits, within 3 s". Under a hung target thread that is not strictly true, because the bound only holds while SetFocus returns. That is a minor imprecision in a recorded claim, not a wrong correction.

One error in the finding's evidence: it cites hv-4 trace lines 78783 to 78797, but hv-4__guest-results__proof__diag-focus-trace.txt has only 1108 lines. finding.title: SettleKeyboardFocus retries a focused window inside the owned window held by a non-member process as 'not yet' instead of failing it as an owned invariant
finding.claim: SettleKeyboardFocus is a new caller of Members(). It gives one label, "outside owned window", to two different cases: focus that is genuinely not in the owned window (transient), and focus in a child of the owned window that belongs to a process outside the retained job (a containment breach). The breach is retried with held=IntPtr.Zero until the 3 s bound, then raised as InvalidOperationException "Owned WebView2 keyboard focus did not settle; last: outside owned window". Everywhere else in the driver, a node inside the owned window that belongs to a non-member is an OwnedInvariantException that fails at once (Names: "Accessibility node outside retained job"; OwnedControl, ShellUnique and ShellTree likewise).
finding.evidence: Line 108: `kind=(focusThread!=0&&(focus==hwnd||IsChild(hwnd,focus))&&new HashSet<uint>(Members()).Contains(focusPid))?WindowClass(focus):"outside owned window";`, followed by `} else held=IntPtr.Zero;` and the 3 s `InvalidOperationException` refusal. Compare lines 258-259 (Names) and 274-275 (OwnedControl), which throw OwnedInvariantException for non-member nodes.
finding.failure_scenario: Win32 focus is on a descendant of the owned HWND whose process is not in the job. The ownership breach is spent as 'not yet' for 3 s and then reported with a generic, ambiguous label and the transient exception type. It still fails closed, because Keys and ShellKeys are not wrapped in any outer retry, so this is not a false pass. Only the exact invariant cause and type are lost.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding holds up, but it is minor.

**What the code does.** In scripts/windows11/windows11_owned.cs line 108, `kind` is set to `WindowClass(focus)` only when three things are all true: `focusThread!=0`, the focus is `hwnd` or a child of it (`IsChild`), and the focus PID is in `Members()`. Every other case gets the same label, "outside owned window". So a live child of the owned HWND that belongs to a process outside the job is labelled the same way as focus that is genuinely elsewhere. That label then goes to `} else held=IntPtr.Zero;` (line 122). It is retried every 10 ms until the 3 s deadline, and line 124 then throws `InvalidOperationException("Owned WebView2 keyboard focus did not settle; last: outside owned window")`.

**Why it is inconsistent.** Elsewhere the driver fails a node from a process outside the job at once with `OwnedInvariantException`:
- `Names` (line 266)
- `OwnedControl` (line 282)
- `OwnedPopupItem` (line 340)
- `ShellUnique` (line 542)
- `ShellTree` (lines 565 and 606)

The diagnostic label is also wrong for this case: the window is inside the owned window, not outside it.

**Why it is not BLOCKING.**
- **Fails closed.** The 3 s deadline is strict. The only `return` is the keyboard-window branch after a 250 ms quiet interval. There is no pass on timeout.
- **No outer retry.** `KeyboardCheckAgain`, `KeyboardQuit` and `ShellKeys` are called directly in windows11_guest.ps1 (lines 214, 221, 231-233, 249-250, 254, 450 and 477). None is inside a `NotYet`/`ShellWait`/`Settles` loop. The exception goes straight to the top-level catch (line 485), which records FAIL with `error_type=System.InvalidOperationException`.
- **No recorded claim is false.** KI-0184 says only that the keyboard window "must be inside the owned window and belong to a current job member". The code enforces that as the condition for accepting focus. The test comment in test_windows11_guest_driver.py also pins this as intended ("Only a window inside the owned window, of a current job member, is classified"). Nothing claims that a foreign child fails as an owned invariant.

So what is lost is only the exact cause, the exception type and up to 3 s.

**Why a plain reclassification would be wrong.** The focus PID is read (line 107) and `IsChild` is checked before `Members()` is called. A member that exits completely between those reads would show up as a non-member child. If that were thrown as an invariant, this race would produce a false owned-invariant failure. A correct fix must re-check the window after `Members()` returns, confirming it still exists with the same thread and PID and is still a child. Only then may it throw `OwnedInvariantException`. As written, the code cannot tell the race apart from a breach.

Verdict: a real but NON_BLOCKING defect, covering the classification and the diagnostic label.

I could not refute this finding. The code does what the finding says.

1. In scripts/windows11/windows11_owned.cs at line 108, one condition joins three tests: `focusThread!=0`, `(focus==hwnd||IsChild(hwnd,focus))` and `Members().Contains(focusPid)`. Any failure becomes the same label, "outside owned window". So Win32 focus on a real descendant of the owned HWND whose PID is not in the job gets the same result as focus that is simply elsewhere. Line 122 then resets `held`, and line 124 stops only at the 3 s `FocusSettleMilliseconds` bound, with an InvalidOperationException whose message ends "last: outside owned window".

2. The rest of the driver treats a non-member node inside the owned window as an ownership breach and throws OwnedInvariantException at once. Examples: Names at line 266, OwnedControl at 282, ShellUnique at 542, ShellMainFocused at 565, and the ShellTree loop at 606. The same function even does this for a structural mismatch, at line 112 ("Owned WebView2 keyboard window required"). The code already knows the IsChild result when it builds the label, so it could tell the two cases apart and does not. This breaks the binding rule that owned-invariant failures must not be retried as 'not yet'.

3. Is the case actually reachable as a breach rather than a harmless race? A member mid-exit makes Members() throw "Owned job member exit in progress", which is the transient path at line 109, not this branch. A destroyed focus window makes GetWindowThreadProcessId return 0. Job membership is inherited when a child process is created, so a WebView2 child process is never briefly outside the job. That leaves only a real cross-process child of the owned window held by a non-member as the way to reach this label while IsChild is true.

Any exception therefore reaches the top-level catch at line 485 and records a FAIL. A lasting breach fails closed. Only the exception type in failure.json and the specific cause are lost. In addition, if a foreign child takes focus briefly and focus then returns to a member keyboard window for 250 ms within the 3 s bound, the breach is ignored and the keys are sent. Even then, input only ever goes to a member-owned Chrome_WidgetWin_1 inside the owned window, so no input is misdirected and no campaign PASS claim becomes false.

The test at test_windows11_guest_driver.py:784-785 pins the current combined expression; it does not assert that a breach throws an invariant.

Verdict: a real inconsistency with the project's owned-invariant rule. It fails closed, so it is NON_BLOCKING.

Even if handles did exist, [GC]::Collect() without [GC]::WaitForPendingFinalizers() would not close finalizable SafeRegistryHandles before the unload.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the finding against the code and it holds. In scripts/windows11/windows11_bootstrap.ps1, lines 111 to 126, the Default hive is loaded, written and unloaded only by `& reg.exe load/add/unload` child processes. Its relaunch-related assertions are Policy::default() accepted and startup_timeout 10_001 refused. Every other RestartOwner relaunch test uses harness() with initial == startup == 50 ms (restart.rs:588-594). That leaves the relaunch bound pinned only by the supervisor-level test relaunch_bound_still_includes_preflight_and_prevents_late_spawn, which calls start_until directly (supervisor.rs:1296). The finding's facts are accurate, but they don't show that the test name or the KI-0182 sentence is false.

1. The relaunch half of the new test does more than repeat an existing check. HEAD's restart.rs had no test that exercises the restart.rs:134 cap. Searching `git show HEAD:.../restart.rs` finds no `10_001` and no Policy with startup_timeout above 10 s. The only use of Policy::default() at HEAD is in recovery_policy_cannot_expand_the_reviewed_bounds, which expects a refusal because of a bad RecoveryPolicy. The new test adds two checks. finding.title: KI-0182 timings overstate what was measured and omit that HV VMs met the 10 s bound
finding.claim: Line 108 says "about 20 s after launch" and "In round 42 the service process appeared 5 to 7 s after the desktop process, so the cold service had about 3 to 5 s to send READY". Line 112 says "With the 5 to 7 s preflight and spawn measured in round 42, the cold first start needs about 13 to 15 s". supervisor.rs:45 and README row 42 repeat the 5 to 7 s figure.
finding.evidence: Only one round 42 VM (host-terminal) ever showed the service process. Its diag-procs.txt has desktop first seen at 6279 ms and japp-orchestrator at 12959 ms, with samples about 2.2 s apart. That gives 6.7 s, bounded 4.5 to 8.8 s. This is the gap between the desktop process and the service process appearing, which includes desktop init, not a preflight measurement. The deadline starts at Supervisor::start, not at process launch, so '3 to 5 s left' is an inference. The 'Local service failed' title appeared 13.8 to 19.9 s after launch (launched at 42.8 s; title between 56.6 and 62.7 s), and 12.4 to 14.1 s after launch in r44 host-nowhesvc. The '13 to 15 s' figure double-counts the 1.3 s spawn included in svcfirst's 7.6 s. Every HV VM in rounds 43-47 (15 VMs) reached Ready under the existing 10 s bound, with the service appearing 1.0 to 3.3 s after the desktop; the KI does not mention this.
finding.failure_scenario: A HIGH product change (a 30 s first-start bound) is justified by figures presented as measured preflight times on 'a cold Windows 11 machine'. In fact they are sampled process-appearance gaps on un-enlightened nested VMs only, and the configuration the campaign now uses does not reproduce the failure.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. Every number it gives checks out against the evidence, and so do its main points about the wording. None of this changes whether the correction is right.

What I checked:

1. **Round 42 host-terminal process timing.** This was the only round 42 VM where japp-orchestrator ever appeared. In host-conhost and pmuoff-conhost only `desktop` appears before the logs end. In host-terminal's diag-procs.txt, the samples before and at the desktop's first sighting are t_ms=4147 and 6279. The samples before and at the service's first sighting are 10737 and 12959. That gives a point estimate of 6.68 s and a bound of 4.46 to 8.81 s. The figure is the gap between two processes appearing in Get-Process.

2. **What that gap includes.** In lib.rs `setup()`, a lot happens before `service.start_background()` runs: the WebviewWindowBuilder builds the window, then `configured_runtime`, `ManagedService::new`, `install_shell_quit_menu` and `diagnostics::create_engine`. Only after that does the worker call `start_initial` and then `Supervisor::start`, which takes the deadline before preflight (supervisor.rs `start_within`). The msedgewebview2 children show up in the same sample as desktop. So the gap includes desktop startup work done before the deadline is taken. Despite that, KNOWN_ISSUES.md:112 calls it "the 5 to 7 s preflight and spawn measured in round 42", and the supervisor.rs:44-46 doc comment says the VM "needed about 5 to 7 s for the runtime-integrity preflight and spawn". Neither is what round 42 measured. KNOWN_ISSUES.md:108's "so the cold service had about 3 to 5 s" is also an inference that assumes `Supervisor::start` ran when desktop.exe was created.

3. **"About 20 s after launch."** In diag-progress.txt, launched is at at_ms=42820. `OwnedApp.Start` only calls CreateProcess, assigns the job and resumes, so this is the process creation time. The diag-ready.ndjson rows show "Starting local service" at 56645 and "Local service failed" at 62694. So the failure came 13.8 to 19.9 s after launch, and 20 s is the top of that window. Round 40 ignore-terminal has no title evidence. Round 44 host-nowhesvc, which is not mentioned in KI-0182, failed 12.4 to 14.1 s after launch (54069 and 55718 against 41655).

4. **Double counting.** svcfirst's diag-service-cold.json starts its stopwatch before `Process.Start` and records spawn_ms=1276 and first_bytes_ms=7603. Under the KI's own labels, spawn is therefore counted in both the round 42 "preflight and spawn" figure and the 7.6 s. The 13 to 15 s total is overstated by up to about 1.3 s.

5. **Hyper-V-enlightened VMs left out.** I checked qemu-argv.json for rounds 43 to 47. Seventeen VMs used the hv-* CPU flags. Two froze in Setup (r44 hv-a and r46 hv-3, KI-0183). The other 15 all recorded ready-ok. All of them ran the same package, 5700fefc…, which still has the 10 s bound, so they reached Ready on the old first start. Their desktop-to-service gaps run from 1.04 to 3.28 s. The only failures were on VMs with plain `-cpu host`. KI-0182 never says that the configuration the campaign now uses does not reproduce the failure.

Why NON_BLOCKING: the core claims hold. The deadline does include the preflight (verified in code). The cold service on its own took 7.6 s to READY. Three VMs without the enlightenments failed under the 10 s bound. Even with corrected arithmetic, the total is still above 10 s: about 11.3 to 13.3 s once the spawn double count is removed, and failures were also observed directly.

So the 30 s first-start bound is not invalidated, and none of this produces a false pass or touches safety. What is wrong is the wording. Approximate process-appearance gaps are presented as measured preflight-and-spawn times, "about 20 s" is the top of a 13.8 to 19.9 s window, and the KI does not mention that all 15 product launches on Hyper-V-enlightened VMs succeeded. That last point matters because a campaign in the current configuration will not exercise the corrected first-start path in a way that shows the fix works.

Suggested fix: in KNOWN_ISSUES.md:108/112, supervisor.rs:44-46 and README row 42, reword these figures as approximate, sampled process-appearance gaps (about 6.7 s, bounded 4.5 to 8.8 s) that include desktop setup. Give the failure-title window as 13.8 to 19.9 s. Add that the 15 launches on Hyper-V-enlightened VMs reached Ready under 10 s.

I checked the evidence myself and the finding holds. Its main conclusion stands, but the numbers behind it are imprecise, and part of the evidence is left out.

findings.title: Every rehearsal VM from round 42 on ran with BitLocker device encryption prevented, a target-OS change the corrected bootstrap does not make, and no document says so
findings.claim: From round 42 on, the diagnostic bootstrap in every rehearsal VM set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\BitLocker PreventDeviceEncryption=1 (the DIAG-NOBITLOCKER marker). The corrected scripts/windows11/windows11_bootstrap.ps1 does not set it, and without it Windows encrypted the OS volume. So every Hyper-V-enlightened measurement behind the KI-0178/0179/0181/0182/0184/0185 resolutions comes from an OS configuration the corrected campaign will not run. The README nonetheless calls each VM's controller 'the candidate correction plus diagnostic instrumentation', and KNOWN_ISSUES and the README never mention BitLocker or device encryption.

That line is present in every retained diag-bootstrap.ps1 of rounds 42-44 and absent in rounds 38-40. In every round 42-47 diag-inputs.json, dropped_markers lists SVCFIRST/NODPS/NODIAGTRACK/NOWHESVC but never NOBITLOCKER, and round47 guest-driver-vs-2100780.diff line 29 carries it. Every round 42-47 forensics.log shows `nbd0p3 ntfs 78.9G Windows`. All three round 40 forensics logs (no prevention) show `nbd0p3 BitLocker 78.9G`, and none of them could read Minidump or evtx. findings.failure_scenario: The released campaign VM runs the corrected bootstrap.
